summary: This document is a hypothesis card (N10) proposing a pre-registered assay to test whether a selective MAO-A inhibitor (clorgyline-class) fails to match methylene blue (MB) in rescuing memory retention on a cytochrome oxidase (COX)-inhibitor amnestic model. The claim is NEGATIVE (predicted failure of selective MAO-A-i to match MB rescue), and the experiment has NOT been run. The document distinguishes this hypothesis from related prior cards (N5–N9) and identifies the key gap: no published head-to-head (H2H) comparison of selective MAO-A-i vs. MB on the COX-amnestic retention panel exists.

content_blocks.title: Claim / Hypothesis Statement
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered cytochrome-oxidase / COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay where parent methylene blue (MB) restores memory, a selective MAO-A inhibitor (clorgyline-class) fails to match that rescue — retention Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside a pre-registered MB-equivalence band). Status label: NEGATIVE. Execution status: NOT_RUN.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Why It Matters
content_blocks.content: Tests the competing 'mild-MAO frame' on the Gonzalez-Lima COX-amnestic assay. If metabolic-memory rescue is MAO-A-owned, a selective MAO-A-i should match parent MB; if rescue requires parent redox/COX-facing chemistry, selective MAO-A-i should fail. Distinct from N5 (selective MAO-A-i ≠ MB on generic WM), N8 (Azure B on COX-amnestic), and N9 (redox-dead on COX-amnestic) — none ran a selective MAO-A drug on the COX-amnestic panel. Soft-claims: selective MAOI ∩ COX-amnestic H2H soft-complete = 0; sole adjacent PMID 40996208 is MAO-B non-match; H2H remains UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Redox-vs-MAO assumption-kill on the COX-amnestic/metabolic-memory class. Parent MB restores retention after COX inhibition and is a potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor; clorgyline-class selective MAO-A-i elevates monoamines in disease models but has no published COX-amnestic retention H2H vs MB. Competing caveat: MAO occupancy/exposure matching — underperformance could reflect under-dosing relative to MB's MAO potency rather than a true mechanistic distinction.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Baseline
content_blocks.content:
1. PMID 12384216 (Callaway/Gonzalez-Lima 2002): Low-dose MB restores spatial memory retention impaired by a cytochrome oxidase inhibitor — no selective-MAOI arm.
2. PMID 21087672 / PMC3026638 (Rojas/Gonzalez-Lima 2011): MB beneficial network effects in an amnestic model (metabolic/network framing) — no selective-MAOI arm.
3. PMID 17721552 / PMC2078225 (Ramsay 2007): MB potent reversible MAO-A inhibition (serotonin-toxicity prediction) — enzyme prior, not COX-amnestic H2H.
4. PMID 26825854 (2016): Clorgyline (selective MAO-A-i) elevates monoamines and improves disease-model endpoints — MAO-A tool prior, not COX-amnestic retention vs MB.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat N5–N9 as proving N10 — N5 left COX-amnestic untested; N8/N9 ran metabolite/redox-dead arms, not a selective MAO-A drug; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated selective-MAOI failure on COX-amnestic.
2. MAO IC50 ≠ brain rescue PD — Ramsay is enzyme inhibition; clorgyline (PMID 26825854) is monoamine elevation/disease model; neither is COX-amnestic retention vs MB.
3. Occupancy matching — underperformance could be under-dosing relative to MB's MAO potency; assay MAO occupancy/monoamine readout without a dosing card; use the same COX-inhibitor amnestic class where parent MB restores. No dosing established.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three critical dependencies identified:
1. Removal of same COX-amnestic/retention contrast of selective MAO-A-i vs parent MB: Without behavioral H2H on the Gonzalez-Lima class assay, MB rescue LITERATURE and MAO-A tool LITERATURE cannot show selective MAO-A-i fails to match MB rescue.
2. Removal of selective MAO-A identity (clorgyline-class) with parent-MB MAO-A framing: Without a verified selective MAO-A tool, underperformance is just 'weak monoaminergic drug,' not an assumption-kill of MAO-owned COX-amnestic rescue.
3. Removal of N5–N9≠proof + soft-complete-empty≠failure + MAO-IC50≠brain-PD + occupancy-matching discipline: Treating N5/N8/N9 or empty/MAO-B-adjacent PubMed or Ramsay/clorgyline enzyme-disease priors as already deciding selective-MAOI COX-amnestic failure would invent a negative result left UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: Refuted if: On the pre-registered COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay, the selective MAO-A-i matches parent MB within the MB-equivalence band (retention Δ >70% of MB or inside band) — especially under exposure/MAO-occupancy-matched conditions — so MAO-necessity for metabolic-memory rescue survives and redox-required rescue fails.

content_blocks.title: Execution & IP Status
content_blocks.content: Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Related prior: N5–N9 (selective MAOI×WM / Azure B / redox-dead ≠ selective-MAOI×COX-amnestic proof). Kill cost tier: 1. Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Vault hold: no. Method: propose-assay.

key_findings: Hypothesis N10 is a NEGATIVE prediction (NOT_RUN): a selective MAO-A inhibitor (clorgyline-class) is predicted to fail to match methylene blue (MB) rescue on a COX-inhibitor amnestic retention assay (retention Δ ≤70% of MB).

No published head-to-head (H2H) comparison of selective MAO-A-i vs. MB on the COX-amnestic retention panel exists (soft-complete = 0); the sole adjacent reference (PMID 40996208) is a MAO-B non-match, not MAO-A.

Literature baseline confirms MB restores spatial memory retention after COX inhibition (PMID 12384216) and has potent reversible MAO-A inhibition (PMID 17721552), but neither study includes a selective-MAOI comparator arm.
Clorgyline is validated as a selective MAO-A tool (PMID 26825854) but only in disease-model monoamine endpoints, not in COX-amnestic retention vs. MB.
Key confound: underperformance of selective MAO-A-i could reflect under-dosing relative to MB's MAO potency rather than a true mechanistic distinction — MAO occupancy/exposure matching is required.
N5–N9 (prior cards on generic WM, Azure B, redox-dead arms) do not constitute proof of N10's claim; the COX-amnestic × selective-MAOI H2H remains genuinely UNKNOWN.
Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; kill cost tier: 1 (low cost experiment).
TRL assessment: TRL 1 — concept/hypothesis only; no experimental data generated; assay proposed but not executed.
